scope: Only the supplied-coefficient, static finite-shell formal transfer kernel. Isotropic boundaries, no stellar beam, no moving medium, no self-consistent saturation. These tests do not solve an atmosphere or certify any application-specific angular resolution.
implementation: Finite impact-parameter panels at every shell edge; tangent-regularizing map; exact segment means from the existing exponential weights; actual shell volume retained. Rays that miss the absorbing core pass through the far hemisphere. Signed extinction is accepted without a floor; nonfinite fields and failed conservation/geometric-volume checks are rejected.

execution.command: taskset -c 55 env JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=src:/tmp/exojax-spectrum-upstream/src /home/kawahara/miniconda3/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_spherical_radiation.py -q

independent_controls: Transparent core angular dilution and constant luminosity agree with closed-form solid-angle/volume integrals.
Uniform thermal field at opacity0,1e-8,1,1e8 remains stationary.
Homogeneous full-sphere mean and outgoing flux agree with independent SciPy chord integrals for negative and positive extinction.
Transparent emission and its signed-opacity derivative agree with analytic values; centered finite differences cross zero opacity.
The volume-weighted Green operator obeys reciprocity with both optically thick and inverted shells.
A deliberately coarse geometric quadrature fails; gain overflow is rejected without clipping.
limitations: No full coupled line, population, thermal, wind or observer result is inferred.
Energy conservation and geometric-volume accuracy do not imply angular convergence of the radiation field.
The common native continuum uses a different geometry; replacement requires explicitly matched source/receiver accounting and complete re-solution.
